basecaller.note: inference data should be basecalled with this model. A different basecaller is a domain shift on the k-mer residual: contrasts between arms that share one basecaller remain valid, absolute charged fractions do not.

anchor.description: sample `left` of the window is the FIRST raw sample of the base at reference position (index of CCAGGC) + 3 — the adapter G that follows CCA. Mapped via the move table (Remora convention: move_position * stride + ts).
anchor.reference_note: any reference whose records carry ...CCA + GGCTTCTTCTTGCTCTT; the 13 nt after the common arm may differ (library adapters vary) and are never read — see masking below.

abstain.aligner_arm_depth_definition: the deepest common-arm offset (>= +1 from the junction) that the ALIGNER placed exactly -- i.e. `q(junction+o) == o` in the reference->query map, before any slop backfill. 0 means bwa placed no arm base at all. Note this is NOT the same as the window being short: with count_arm_bases the features are computed by walking the query, so a read with aligner_arm_depth 0 still HAS arm features -- they simply do not discriminate (balanced accuracy 0.4993 on that population, 100% of the uncharged library called charged). Abstention keys on the aligner's reach for exactly that reason.
abstain.emit: no-call (absent cl tag / null score), NOT a default class
abstain.why: the read is untrustworthy, not merely incomplete. Giving it real arm features (by counting) does not help: on that population the model scores balanced accuracy 0.4993 and calls 100% of the uncharged library charged. The population is also physically distinct -- at MATCHED translocation speed it is 14-45x enriched in the charged library, across every isodecoder, every channel and every quarter of the run -- which is consistent with these reads being charged, but is not established as such while label and flowcell are confounded
abstain.reporting: report the no-call RATE beside any charging fraction. Arm resolvability is charging-correlated, so a fraction computed over called reads only is an UNDERESTIMATE -- the same bias the remora cca_classifier has, differing only in being declared

resolution.how: for arm offsets 1..N, the query position is q(junction) + o -- walked along the query, NOT looked up in the alignment. Soft-clipped bases still carry move-table spans, so this works past the end of the alignment. Offsets above N are unresolved for every read (NaN).
resolution.why: with the aligner-derived rule, feature availability in the arm depended on how far bwa got, and bwa stops at the adduct: 20.9-25.3% of charged-library reads lost the entire arm against 0.9% of uncharged. The model read that missing pattern as a class.

features.layout: per base, offsets outer and stats inner, matching `order`
features.anchor_offset: b+0 is the adapter G at reference index(CCAGGC)+3; negative offsets run into the tRNA body, positive into the common arm

per_base.dwell: samples the move table assigns to the base
per_base.mean: mean of the read-normalised signal over the base
per_base.resid: mean minus the base's expected k-mer level, where the expectation is z-scored across the read's valid levels. This is the feature that carries the signal -- computing it against a different k-mer table gives a different feature space and an invalid model

features.normalisation: per READ median/MAD (1.4826), not per window: a window-level gauge subtracts the level shift being measured
features.mask: bases before the common arm are never read; the arm is GGCTTCTTCTTGCTCTT and the 13 nt after it differ between library adapters
features.missing: NaN where a base did not align; the GBM handles NaN natively

kmer_table.note: versioned dependency: the residual is defined relative to it

refinement.meaning: empty = rough-rescale only (gauge, no DP). Otherwise a banded DP refines the mapping; mask_before/after exclude that span from its cost so the arm is not fitted to levels that are wrong at the adduct. Masking WITHOUT an anchored flank collapses dwell to 0.

metrics.label_source: Library chemistry, not a model. ldx01-05 chemical ligation only, which joins the adapter to the amino acid's alpha-amine and so cannot happen on a deacylated molecule; ldx11-16 enzymatic ligation only, which needs a free 3'-OH a charged tRNA lacks. Reads are assigned to blocks by an LDX barcode call (barcode_crf_nbc16_rna004@v0.3.0), and that caller's error is the only label noise: ~9.3% of the ldx01-05 label is foreign by the 5' marker, against ~0.2% for ldx11-16.
metrics.split: held-out flowcell; training draw matched within (run x isotype x speed bin) across the two chemically pure blocks

standardisation.method: per-channel affine over the TRAIN split's observed values

geometry.anchor: alignment junction (adapter-G base start), per-base features

metrics.coverage_note: Reads whose common arm did not align (cs_source == junction_fallback) are excluded here and abstained on at inference: their whole left window is masked and every arm feature is NaN, and a model scored on them answers ~100% charged whatever the library. The exclusion rate is far higher for charged reads, so any charging fraction derived from called reads alone is an UNDERESTIMATE. Report the no-call rate beside it.
metrics.note: Labels are library chemistry: chemical ligation attaches the adapter to the amino acid's alpha-amine and cannot happen on a deacylated molecule, enzymatic ligation needs a free 3'-OH a charged tRNA lacks. The training draw is matched on isotype and translocation speed because the two blocks also differ in 5' adapter and run ~53% apart. Test is a held-out flowcell.

operating_point.source: MEASURED ON THE v6.0.0 CORPUS with this model's own shipped checkpoint; nothing here is carried over from charging_feature_nn_rna004. benchmarks/ldx16x_sup6/charging_operating_point/sweep.json, via `charging_gauge_block` + `charging_operating_point --by-run --no-gate`. Measured against CHEMISTRY rather than labels, on the full natural populations. Pooled at cl>=200: FPR 1.623% on the enzymatic-only library (ldx11-16, n=13,673,568, 0% charged by ligation chemistry) = 1 false call in 62; TPR 0.9103 on the chemical-only library (ldx01-05, n=1,788,383, 100% charged, corrected for demux contamination at --gold-purity 0.907). QUOTE REP2, the held-out flowcell -- rep1 trained the model: rep2 FPR 1.549%, TPR 0.9073 (rep1 1.697% / 0.9133; replicate spread 0.0015 FPR, 0.0060 TPR). The reproduction gate is OFF by necessity: it targets charging_feature_nn_rna004's published numbers, and this model is not meant to reproduce them. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM v5.3.0 AT THE SAME cl -- FPR 1.62% against 1.74% and TPR 0.910 against 0.939, i.e. cl=200 is strictly MORE CONSERVATIVE on v6.0.0: higher purity, ~2.9pp less yield. cl=200 is kept so the family shares one convention, but note that NO cl reproduces both v5 numbers -- matching its FPR needs cl~195 (TPR still 0.917) and matching its TPR needs cl~176 (FPR 2.15%, 24% worse). That is not calibration drift, it is the -0.0044 AUROC ranking loss of the v6 feature space showing up in the threshold; see dev-notes/basecaller-domain-shift.md. CAVEAT (unchanged, escapepod-models#63) -- precision depends on the SAMPLE's charged fraction, not on the model, so a single threshold does not carry across samples whatever the basecaller. On this model: 95% precision needs cl>=128 at f=0.50, cl>=159 at f=0.34, cl>=202 at f=0.25 and cl>=247 at f=0.10; 99% is unreachable below f~0.25.

caveats: Headline accuracy is metrics.test_cross_experiment (20240928 runs). Within-experiment val is optimistic: in 20240729 each class is one whole flowcell, so val cannot separate charging from batch.
Trained on S. cerevisiae tRNA with the edx01/edx02 adapter family. Reads whose common arm differs from GGCTTCTTCTTGCTCTT are out of distribution.

The operating point is `cl >= 200` and is a RECOMMENDATION measured on held-out data, not a property of the model. Its precision and recall are in metrics; a caller wanting a different precision should move it and say so.

Metrics are computed over reads the model will actually score, i.e. after the `abstain` rule. Reads it abstains on are excluded from training and evaluation alike; their rate is label-correlated and is reported per class in the corpus summary (excluded_collapsed).

This is the per-base-feature ONNX variant. `escpod signal classify` reads it from escapepod-rs#231 onward, which added `feature_model` beside `gbm` and runs the graph over the flat vector the runtime already builds. An escpod predating that PR refuses the bundle with `missing field `gbm``, so pin the runtime version alongside it.

input.name: features
input.fold: `features.order` is offsets-outer / channels-inner, so the k-th selected column is offset k // 2, value channel k % 2. Transpose to [channel, offset].

standardisation.method: per-channel affine over the TRAIN split's observed values
standardisation.apply: value channel c = observed ? (x - mu[c]) / sd[c] : 0.0; observed channel c = observed ? 1.0 : 0.0, where `observed` means the selected feature is finite
standardisation.why: constants fitted on the TRAIN split's observed values and shipped rather than recomputed: a per-batch gauge would make one read's answer depend on which reads it was run beside, and recomputing over unresolved bases (zero-filled, not absent) would move the gauge by whatever fraction of the input happens to be unresolved

feature_model.missing: NaN is NOT passed to the network. Unlike the GBM, which handles missingness natively, this model is told about it explicitly: the value channel is zeroed and the paired observed channel carries the indicator. Feeding NaN straight through gives NaN logits.
